correctness.rationale: Direct F^2=(h(x),h(y)) and F^4=(h²(x),h²(y)); h decreasing and h² increasing bounded, so every scalar orbit converges to fixed point of h². Hyperbolic scalar two-cycle coordinates L=r e^-s,H=r e^s reduce to unique increasing B_m(s) from strict Q(t)=t*coth(t) convexity; bifurcation threshold b_c and multiplier (m*sinh(s)/sinh(ms))²<1 follow. Scalar sign basins give exactly two primitive planar four-cycles, no others, and support of invariant measures via recurrence. At b=b_c, symbolic expansion of normalized h² yields z ↦ z − (m²−1)z³/6+O(z⁴); reciprocal-square telescoping proves signed sqrt(n) four-phase law. Independently recomputed cubic coefficient for m=2,3,4,7 exactly, and checked source finite script; these checks do not prove universal real m.
